verses.sa: धृतराष्ट्र उवाचधर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
verses.tr: Dhritarashtra says: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra and eager for battle?
verses.angle: Mamakah: the word that splits a family
verses.speaker: Dhritarashtra

intro.text: A blind king waits in his palace and asks a single question about the two armies gathering on the field.

body.text: Dhritarashtra says: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra and eager for battle? Mamakah means my own. The Pandavas are his brother's sons, raised in his own house, and with that one word he splits the family into mine and theirs. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचदृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Seeing the Pandava army arranged in battle formation, King Duryodhana went to Dronacharya and spoke these words.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya answers the king's question by turning to his son Duryodhana. Listen to the very first person Duryodhana approaches.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Seeing the Pandava army arranged in battle formation, King Duryodhana went to Dronacharya and spoke these words. The verse says Duryodhana approached his teacher, Drona, and spoke. He does not go to his own grandfather, Bhishma, or to King Duryodhana, but to his military preceptor, the first person he trusts to speak to. Duryodhana points to the Pandava army and asks Drona to look at it.

verses.sa: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् । व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥
verses.tr: O teacher, look at this great army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle formation by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.
verses.angle: Drona's own student commands the enemy
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Duryodhana stands before his commander and points to the enemy lines. He names exactly who leads them.

body.text: O teacher, look at this great army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle formation by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada. Duryodhana calls him Acharya, your teacher, while pointing to the enemy lines. He reminds Drona that the enemy commander is his own wise student, Dhrishtadyumna, turning a report into a personal challenge. Then Duryodhana lists the great warriors standing in the Pandava army, matching strength against strength.

verses.sa: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि । युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥
verses.tr: Here in the Pandava army are mighty warriors, great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Satyaki, Virata, and the great chariot-warrior Drupada.
verses.angle: Duryodhana names the Pandava army's best
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Duryodhana stands before Drona and lists the strongest fighters in the enemy camp.

body.text: Here in the Pandava army are mighty warriors, great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Satyaki, Virata, and the great chariot-warrior Drupada. He names Satyaki, Virata, and Drupada, calling them equal to Bhima and Arjuna. Sanjaya then continues with the names of Drupada's sons and the kings from Kashi and other lands.

verses.sa: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् । पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥
verses.tr: Dhृष्टकेतु, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men.
verses.angle: Purujit and Kuntibhoja, kin on both sides
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Duryodhana is naming the Pandava commanders one by one. Listen for the two brothers who are also his own uncle's family.

body.text: Dhृष्टकेतु, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men. The roll call keeps growing: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya. Sanjaya then lists even more warriors, bringing the total number to seven.

verses.sa: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् । सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥
verses.tr: Yudhamanyu, brave and powerful, Uttamaujas, brave and powerful, Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi, all of them are great warriors.
verses.angle: Subhadra's son and Draupadi's sons stand with the Pandavas
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Duryodhana keeps naming the enemy's best fighters. Listen to how he names the sons of Subhadra and Draupadi.

body.text: Yudhamanyu, brave and powerful, Uttamaujas, brave and powerful, Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi, all of them are great warriors. Listen to one word, sauhadrashcha, Subhadra's son. The Pandavas are not fighting alone; Subhadra's son and Draupadi's sons stand beside them, so the enemy line reads like a full family under arms. Duryodhana then turns from the enemy to name the great warriors on his own side.

verses.sa: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम । नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
verses.tr: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army.
verses.angle: Pride counts its own strength when fear is near.
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Duryodhana finishes naming the enemy and now turns to his own side. Listen to how he presents his commanders to Drona.

body.text: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army. He calls Drona dvijottama, best of the twice-born, and then says he names these chiefs just to remind him of them. The word reminds him of the army he leads. Duryodhana lists Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa as the pillars of his army.

verses.sa: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः । अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥
verses.tr: Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta are also there.
verses.angle: Names as a shield for fear
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Duryodhana is trying to steady himself by naming the great warriors on his side. Listen for who he calls out.

body.text: Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta are also there. Duryodhana lists Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta's son, as if the names alone could hold his fear. He now moves from naming his commanders to listing the heroes who have already died for him.

verses.sa: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः । नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥
verses.tr: Besides these, many heroes have given up their lives for my sake. They wield many kinds of weapons and are all skilled in warfare.
verses.angle: Tyaktajivitah: the price of his cause
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Duryodhana continues his boast to Drona. He names more of his own side's fighters, and then counts one thing as his real strength.

body.text: Besides these, many heroes have given up their lives for my sake. They wield many kinds of weapons and are all skilled in warfare. Listen to the phrase tyaktajivitah, having given up life, and madarthe, for my sake. These men have already paid the highest price for his cause, and he names their sacrifice as his own strength. Duryodhana then compares the two sides, claiming his force is smaller but still sufficient.

verses.sa: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् । पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥
verses.tr: Our force, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient; their force, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient.
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: Listen for the exact words Duryodhana uses to judge the two armies before the first arrow flies.

body.text: Our force, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient; their force, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient. Duryodhana openly calls his own army insufficient and the Pandava army sufficient. He doubts his strength because Bhishma guards his side, while Bhima guards theirs. He then orders his commanders to protect Bhishma from all sides.

verses.sa: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः । भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥
verses.tr: Remain at your stations on every front and protect Bhishma from all sides.
verses.angle: eva: only, making Bhishma the sole center
verses.speaker: Duryodhana

intro.text: After sizing up the two armies, Duryodhana gives his first command. Listen for how he places one man at the center of the entire battle plan.

body.text: Remain at your stations on every front and protect Bhishma from all sides. Listen to the word eva, only. He does not tell them to protect the army or the king, but to protect only Bhishma, making the grandfather the single pillar holding up every warrior. Sanjaya then tells Dhritarashtra that Bhishma, the grandfather, roars and blows his conch to fill Duryodhana with joy.
